title: Element names of the two delivery outcomes, the carrier of the route state to resume and the values of the owner task are not in the sources
source: RWB-E1-007 sections 4, 9, 11, 12 and 13; P3 context pack (tables, 22 operations, events); FSD P3 A2.3 and TSD P3 v3 T-A.1
description: The legacy story moves the route state and raises the owner task through the in-process interfaces CaseEvents.raise and TaskApi.raiseTask and names no event payload, no carrier for the route state to resume and no value for the task code or the task due date. RWB-P2-E1007-CON is published elsewhere and is not readable for this work package, so the element names of rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1 and rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 that the listener reads, the place where the from route state is held so a delivered file can restore it, and the values of the task code and the due date rule cannot be copied character for character. The story reads the item status through the rwb-integration admin operation, holds the from route state on the latest decision-record entry, and reads the task code and the due date from the task reference rows of rwb-case at the version in force; every such value reads Not specified in the source documents.
evidence: RWB-E1-007 section 12 lists the Java interfaces OutboundFiles, OutboundFileAdapter and IdempotencyGuard with no event schema; section 9 names RESUME_STATE as the target of RETRY_SUCCEEDED without saying where the resumed state is kept; section 11 lists task.case_id, task_code, status and owner_role with no value; section 13 build step 5 says only CaseEvents.raise for four outcomes and TaskApi.raiseTask for the owner task. The P3 context pack lists 15 tables, 22 REST operations, 7 events, 3 jobs and 1 workflow and names no delivery event payload.
owner_role: TechX and the rwb-integration contract owner
proposed: Confirm the payload elements, the resume-state carrier and the task values in RWB-P2-E1007-CON, the rwb-case parameter and reference loads and the Logical Data Model at contract review; rename in this story without changing a value, a rule or a criterion if they differ.

title: The legacy P3 interfaces and the case-action path have no operation in the target case contract
source: RWB-E1-007 section 12 (published interfaces) and section 13 build step 5; RWB-E1-007 section 8 BR1 and section 10 (SY-CASEWF); P3 context pack REST operation list
description: The legacy story moved the route state and raised the task through the published Java interfaces CaseEvents.raise and TaskApi.raiseTask inside one process, and the earlier version of the adapter exposed its exception queue under /api/recovery/v1. In the target, rwb-case publishes 22 operations and none of them is a case-action path or a task-raise path, and a consumed event is not a caller that may be authorised like a person. The story therefore converts both interfaces into internal services of the file-outcome listener, adds no path, and keeps the exception-queue read and the resend with rwb-integration, where the item lives.
evidence: P3 context pack REST operations provided: GET /admin/change-log, GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, GET /admin/parameters, GET /cases, GET /cases/export, GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts, GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action, GET /cases/{caseId}/parties, GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline, GET /cases/{caseId}/timers, GET /me/tasks, GET /queues, GET /queues/{queueId}/cases, PATCH /tasks/{taskId}, POST /admin/reference-loads and its three sub-paths, POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold, POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer, POST /queues/{queueId}/placements. No POST /cases/{caseId}/actions and no task-raise path. RWB-E1-007 section 12 lists the two interfaces and section 13 build step 5 wires them.
proposed: Keep the move internal to the listener as ASM-B2-P3-013-4 records; revisit only if a case-action operation is added to the case contract for another reason, in which case the operation is that story's and this one stays event-driven.
